diagnosis.summary: order-service is experiencing severe Lambda execution slowdown that has persisted for 3 minutes. Mean handler duration rose from 2 ms to 352 ms (176x), and end-to-end latency at both p50 and p95 followed at roughly the same scale. No errors have been recorded and request rate is unchanged.
diagnosis.root_cause: A sharp increase in Lambda handler execution time within order-service is the most likely root cause, with handler CPU time rising 176x from baseline while traffic and error rates remained stable.
evidence: order-service mean Lambda handler duration rose 176x, from 2 ms at baseline to 352 ms currently.
order-service p50 end-to-end latency rose approximately 21x, from 17 ms at baseline to 360 ms currently.
order-service p95 end-to-end latency rose approximately 15.6x, from 24 ms at baseline to 375 ms currently.
order-service request rate is flat at 2.9 rps against a baseline of 2.9 rps.
order-service 5xx error rate remains at 0.0, unchanged from baseline.
recommended_actions: Inspect order-service Lambda CloudWatch Logs for the current window starting 2026-10-30T16:03:00Z to identify any slow operations, timeouts, or unexpected code paths inside the handler.
Check DynamoDB metrics for the order-service table (db_latency_ms_mean, db_latency_ms_p95, throttled_requests) to determine whether database calls are contributing to the handler slowdown.
Review dependency_latency_ms_mean and dependency_error_count for order-service to assess whether calls to payment-service are slower than baseline.
Check cold_start_count for order-service to determine whether Lambda cold starts are contributing to the elevated execution time.
If handler slowdown persists, consider increasing Lambda memory allocation or investigating any recently deployed code changes to order-service.
